'''Hive-Engine''' is the token layer that Hive actually uses, and '''Smart Media Tokens (SMTs)''' are the token layer Steemit announced and the ecosystem waited years for. They are '''not the same thing''', and an earlier revision of this page said they were — it described SMTs as "a key feature of the Hive-Engine ecosystem" and called CURE an SMT. '''Both statements were wrong''', and the correction is the most useful thing on this page, because the gap between the promised layer and the built one is why this whole side of the ecosystem exists.

The short version: '''a Graphene chain will not run your code.''' That one architectural fact — see [[The STEEM HIVE BLURT MELEK VKBT and CURE Matrix|the Matrix]] — forces tokens to live somewhere else, and the story below is the ecosystem working out where.

== 1. Why STEEM needed tokens at all ==

Steem, Hive, Blurt and [[MELEK Blockchain|MELEK]] are Graphene chains. Graphene has a '''fixed operation set''' — `comment`, `vote`, `transfer`, `delegate_vesting_shares` and a few dozen others — and '''no general-purpose virtual machine on layer one'''. You cannot deploy a contract to it. That is a deliberate trade: it is why a post or a vote is a cheap fixed operation and why the chain is '''feeless''', with bandwidth rationed by staked Resource Credits rather than auctioned as gas.

The consequence is unavoidable. A community that wanted its own token — a reward unit for a niche, a game currency, a tipping coin — '''had nowhere to put it.''' The chain that was excellent at social operations could not express "my token, my rules". Every token on this side of the ecosystem exists to fill that hole.

=== Where the two token models came from, and where the witnesses came from ===

The operator was reading both forums while this split formed, and his 2020 account of it is compact and worth quoting because it names the distinction that still organises this wiki: '''"Bitshares had Assets and Ethereum had Tokens."'''

On the Bitshares side, an Asset was '''"not mined but created and owned by the creator, to then be distributed like stocks, or coupons, or tickets"''' — issued rather than earned, and then traded on OpenLedger like any other market. That is the User-Issued Asset, and it is the direct ancestor of every engine token described on this page; see [[Token Buybacks, Market Fees, and the UIA Lineage]].

Two further details from the same account matter for understanding why this ecosystem is shaped the way it is:

* '''The ICO era incubated on the Bitshares forum, and so did Steem's governance.''' '''"Bitsharestalk.org is similar to Bitcointalk.org and is kind of where the ICO trend incubated, and was where the Steemit Witnesses came from."''' The witness set was not assembled from nowhere — it arrived from the chain that had already been running issued assets.
* '''Graphene was the vehicle.''' '''"Bitshares was created by Dan and Ned, on what they named the Graphene Blockchain... And they used Graphene to create Steemit."''' His conclusion then is effectively the thesis MELEK is built on: '''"Steemit is a Graphene Blockchain, which can and should be copied into any website model. Any Forum or City or Charity, etc, could launch a Graphene Blockchain to run their website, have Witnesses and Nodes, a Currency, and Voting."'''

And the consequence, when Steemit Inc. changed hands: the witnesses functioned as a board of directors that the buyer had not accounted for. '''"When Ned sold Steemit INC it started a War with the Witnesses and eventually they forked Steemit... This Platform and Currency are called HIVE. So now there are basically 2 Steemits."''' That fork is why the token layer this page describes ended up on Hive rather than Steem, and why §3 below ends the way it does.

== 2. Smart Media Tokens — the protocol answer that arrived too late ==

Steemit Inc.'s answer was to put tokens '''into the protocol'''. Smart Media Tokens were announced in 2017 with a whitepaper and sustained promotion: each community would get its own token with its own reward pool, running natively on Steem.

What actually happened was delay. Steemit published a schedule for a January 2019 testnet and a '''24 March 2019''' mainnet release, then posted an update on 11 March 2019 delaying SMTs '''to focus on MIRA''' (a memory-reduction project), and later said it was not ready to give a specific timeline at all.<ref>https://steemit.com/steem/@steemitblog/smts-release-dates</ref> A later Steemit press release in 2019 was headlined "Steemit Releases Smart Media Tokens" and described SMTs as having been '''live on testnet for over 40 days'''.<ref>https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/steemit-releases-smart-media-tokens-300967989.html</ref>

Treat the final status carefully: the promotion outran the delivery by years, the Justin Sun acquisition and the Hive fork then reorganised the whole ecosystem, and '''no significant token economy ever ran on SMTs'''. What matters for this wiki is the part that is unambiguous — '''the tokens people actually used were never SMTs.'''

== 3. Steem-Engine — the community answer that shipped, and then died ==

While SMTs were being scheduled and rescheduled, '''Jesse Reich (@aggroed)''' and collaborators built '''Steem-Engine''', launched 2019: a '''side-chain''' where anyone could mint a token and trade it, plus '''Scotbot''', which gave a token its own reward pool and its own front-end tribe.

The launch post is explicit about the distinction this page exists to make: '''"Steem Engine Tokens are different than Smart Media Tokens (SMTs) currently being developed by Steemit, Inc."'''<ref>https://hive.blog/steemengine/@aggroed/introducing-steem-engine-com</ref> It shipped because it did not need the chain's permission — it read ordinary Steem operations and interpreted them off-chain.

Then the March 2020 fork split the ecosystem, and the token layer went with Hive. Steem-side users who had held Steem custodially on Steem-Engine were airdropped Hive, and tribe owners had to rebuy '''BEE''' on Hive-Engine to rebuild their tokens — one estimate put a typical tribe at around '''4,300 BEE'''.<ref>https://hive.blog/hive-engine/@themarkymark/the-future-of-steem-engine-tribes-on-hive-engine</ref> The Steem side then decayed: outages, unresponsive support, ENG holders who felt written off.

'''Steem-Engine no longer exists.''' @aggroed announced its closure in March 2023 under the title "Steem Engine is Closing Down April 30th", and the Steem-side engine was terminated that April.<ref>https://peakd.com/steem-engine/@aggroed/steem-engine-is-closing-down-april-30th</ref><ref>https://propol.is/wiki/Hive-Engine</ref> Anyone reading older documentation that treats steem-engine.net as live is reading history.

== 4. What the Hive-Engine system actually looks like ==

Hive-Engine is the surviving successor, and its design is worth understanding because '''MELEK-Engine is built on the same idea'''.

* '''A side-chain read off layer one.''' Hive-Engine executes smart contracts from data published to Hive — it scans Hive blocks for operations carrying its sidechain ID and runs the contracts those operations describe.<ref>https://propol.is/wiki/Hive-Engine</ref> Hive itself knows nothing about any of it; a token transfer is a `custom_json` to Hive and a state change to the engine. This is '''exactly''' the relationship MELEK-Engine has to MELEK, down to the sidechain id (`mse-mainnet-melek`).
* '''Its own witnesses.''' Engine witnesses verify transactions and produce engine blocks, elected by DPoS with votes weighted by staked '''WORKERBEE'''.<ref>https://propol.is/wiki/Hive-Engine</ref>
* '''BEE''' is the fee token — you spend it to create a token or a pool. Ours is '''APIS''', which works the same way and is '''mined by forever-locking wrapped MELEK''' rather than bought from us. See [[Utilities and Sinks]].
* '''SCOT and tribes.''' Scotbot gives a token a reward pool and a front-end, so a community gets what looks like its own social network with its own currency. LeoFinance, PIZZA's community and dozens of others are tribes in this sense.
* '''Diesel pools''' — the AMM layer, added later. Creating one cost '''1000 BEE''', and notably '''trading fees were not offered at launch''', which left pool creators to find their own way to incentivise liquidity.<ref>http://hiveblog.c0ff33a.uk/hive-engine/@aggroed/hive-engine-weekly-developers-meetings-aggressive-target-live-diesel-pools-by-friday</ref> That omission is instructive: a pool with no fee has no organic reason to exist, which is why [[KulaSwap and the DEX Lineage|KulaSwap]] and [[MWALI|the MWALI gauge]] pay liquidity directly.

A caution on all of the above: the sourcing available is largely '''2021-era''' community posts, and plans described then — such as moving tribe distribution off Scotbot and onto witness-run contracts — may or may not have been completed. Check current Hive-Engine channels before relying on any specific parameter.

== 5. Why this lineage matters to us ==

Read in order it is one story: '''BitShares UIA (2014) → Steem-Engine (2019) → Hive-Engine (2020) → MELEK-Engine (2026)'''. Each step is the same problem — a chain that will not run your code — solved by bolting a token layer alongside it.

The UIA end of that lineage is where the token-management mechanics come from, including buybacks, market fees and fee pools; that is covered in [[Token Buybacks, Market Fees, and the UIA Lineage]].

And one correction to carry forward: '''VKBT and CURE are engine tokens, not SMTs.''' Their peer group is other engine tokens, never the coins with their own chains. Putting a token's market cap next to a coin's is the category error [[The STEEM HIVE BLURT MELEK VKBT and CURE Matrix|the Matrix page]] exists to prevent.

== Coverage ==
Corrects an earlier revision that conflated SMTs with Hive-Engine tokens and called CURE an SMT. Covers why a Graphene chain's fixed op set forces a separate token layer, the SMT announcement-and-delay history, Steem-Engine's launch and its 2023 closure, Hive-Engine's architecture (sidechain reads, WORKERBEE witnesses, BEE fees, SCOT tribes, diesel pools), the Bitshares-Assets-versus-Ethereum-Tokens distinction and the Graphene/witness lineage in the operator's own 2020 words, and the UIA-to-MELEK-Engine lineage. Hive-Engine parameters are sourced from 2021-era community posts and flagged as possibly stale.
